chapter_title: 第169章 應禪溪的特等獎

segments.title: 第169章 應禪溪的特等獎
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Era Chapter 169 Ying Chanxi's Grand Prize

"After all, she was the little hero of Class 8 this morning. As the class president, I still need to give her a little reward as encouragement."

Li Luo said to Ying Chanxi as they walked downstairs, "Besides, I don't really care about the prize draw, so I'll just let her do it."

"Oh." Ying Chanxi didn't mind that, but... he had clearly promised to accompany her this morning.

"Zhusheng, here, this is for you." Ying Chanxi stuffed the stamp booklet in her hand into Yan Zhusheng's, "You can use mine."

"Oh." Yan Zhusheng looked down at the stamp booklet in her hand. The sixteen stamps on it were all neat and tidy, the result of Ying Chanxi's hard work. "Thank you, Xixi."

"You're welcome." Ying Chanxi reached out and snatched the stamp booklet from Li Luo's hand, hugging it to her chest. "Let's go."

Li Luo: "...What's the difference?"

"None of your business."

The three of them went downstairs together and soon arrived at Houde Road.

Three booths had already been set up along the road, serving as the prize draw locations for the first, second, and third years.

"Oh? You're here."

Xu Youyu, who was patrolling and inspecting the area, saw Li Luo's group and waved at them with a smile. "Hurry up and get in line. We're about to hit one hundred people."

The first hundred and the last hundred were separated by two prize draw chances.

As soon as she heard Xu Youyu's reminder, Ying Chanxi quickly pulled Yan Zhusheng to get in line, leaving Li Luo to the side.

"Why aren't you lining up?" Xu Youyu looked at Li Luo with a strange expression.

"My stamp booklet was stolen." Li Luo pointed to the booklet in Ying Chanxi's hand and said innocently, "Madam President, how about you compensate me with a new one?"

"The most I can compensate you with is an empty booklet." Xu Youyu shot him a look, then asked, "Then what about Xixi's own one?"

"It's with Yan Zhusheng."

"And Zhusheng's?"

"She was helping in the classroom all morning, so she didn't get to play at all," Li Luo said. "I'm a kind person, so I gave up my chance at the draw."

"Oh, you're a good person." Xu Youyu nodded.

"Isn't Senior Sister going to give me a consolation prize? Like letting me draw an extra time or something."

"Why are you always thinking about using connections?" Xu Youyu looked speechless. "After the draw ends at noon, if there are any prizes left, you can go take some."

"A prize I didn't win myself is not a prize worth taking."

"...I think you're quite the masochist."

The two of them chatted idly, then moseyed over to the prize draw table. They saw that Yan Zhusheng and Ying Chanxi had already reached the front of the line, handed over their stamp booklets, and successfully got in as part of the first hundred people, receiving 4 chances to draw.

"How about we take turns drawing, one for each of us?" Ying Chanxi was eager to try and suggested to Yan Zhusheng, "You first?"

"Xixi can go first." Yan Zhusheng was very modest.

So Ying Chanxi didn't refuse, reaching her hand into the lottery box. She pulled out a slip of paper and handed it to the student in front who was in charge of the draw.

The student wearing a staff badge took the slip, opened it, and read: "One participation prize."

Another student next to him rummaged through the prize box, pulled out a pack of spicy strips, and handed it to Ying Chanxi. "If you don't like spicy strips, you can exchange them for fruit or something."

"Why didn't you let me exchange it when I wanted to just now?" A girl who had just finished drawing nearby hadn't gone far, and she immediately questioned him.

The boy in charge of giving out prizes broke out in a sweat, looking awkwardly at Ying Chanxi, then at the girl.

"Um... this is fine, no need to exchange." Ying Chanxi was already used to the sudden kindness from boys and naturally declined the offer. She turned her head and said to Yan Zhusheng, "Zhusheng, your turn."

"What prizes are there?" Yan Zhusheng peeked into the prize box on the side and asked curiously.

"The first prize is a fountain pen. There are only three in total, a special custom-made New Year's edition. The second prize is a small pillow that you can slip your hands into, very convenient for napping in the classroom. There are twenty of those in total."

The student in charge of handing out prizes said, "The third prize is a stationery pencil case, there are fifty of those. And then there are participation prizes, which are all small snacks."

"In addition, there is also a grand prize, which is a mystery prize. It will only be announced if it's drawn."

Li Luo listened from the side with great interest. "Why so mysterious? Senior Sister, what's the grand prize? How come I don't know anything about it?"

"There are so many people in the Student Council. If we announced it directly during the meeting, could it still be called a mystery prize?" Xu Youyu said. "You guys just draw it first and then we'll see."

Unfortunately, the Memory Palace was useless when it came to prize draws, so Li Luo didn't bother getting involved, letting Ying Chanxi and Yan Zhusheng have at it.

After listening to the explanation, Yan Zhusheng looked carefully at the prizes, then said, "I like that pillow."

"Even if you like it, you might not be able to draw it," Li Luo chuckled from the side.

But in the next second, Yan Zhusheng had already handed the slip she drew to the student opposite them.

That student unfolded the slip, looked at it, and immediately looked at Li Luo. "Second prize, one pillow."

Li Luo: "?"

"Is your mouth blessed or something?" Xu Youyu looked at him strangely. "Have you been praying to crows?"

"Senior Sister, don't be so harsh," Li Luo's mouth twitched. "Let's see her do it again."

The second draw.

Ying Chanxi got another participation prize, happily receiving a pack of spicy strips.

Yan Zhusheng, however, drew again with a blank expression.

The student opposite them unfolded it, looked, and then looked at Li Luo again. "Second prize, one pillow."

Li Luo: "???"

"Wait... this lottery box can't be rigged, can it?" Li Luo moved closer to the box and examined it again and again, completely baffled.

Xu Youyu, standing to the side, nearly burst out laughing. "Alright, alright, if you say any more, Zhusheng is going to win all the remaining pillows."

"I'm not drawing anymore." Yan Zhusheng shook her head, hugging the two pillows still in their plastic wrap. She stood to the side and said to Li Luo, "I got what I wanted. You can have the remaining two draws."

Li Luo nodded, stood next to Ying Chanxi, and said to her with a smile, "Little puppy, you want to draw first?"

"Hmph." Ying Chanxi puffed out her cheeks and ignored him, drawing for the third time.

Regrettably, it was still a participation prize.

"Your luck isn't very good." Li Luo glanced at the three packs of spicy strips in Ying Chanxi's arms and couldn't help but shake his head.

"You draw then," Ying Chanxi snorted coldly. "Let's see you draw one if you're so good. You think you're Zhusheng or something."

"Fine by me." Li Luo had a nonchalant expression as he reached into the lottery box, casually felt around, and pulled out a slip of paper to hand over.

The student opposite him unfolded it and said, "Third prize, one pencil case."

"See?" Li Luo raised an eyebrow and smiled smugly. "Although my luck isn't as good as Yan Zhusheng's, it's still a tiny bit better than yours."

Ying Chanxi narrowed her eyes at him, her hand gripping the spicy strips so tightly that she really wanted to punch him.

But she took a deep breath, extended her hand once more, and pulled out the final prize slip.

"Huh?" The student opposite them unfolded the paper and was instantly surprised. "Congratulations, you've won our grand prize!"

"Really?" Ying Chanxi's face lit up, and she instantly became happy, slapping Li Luo on the shoulder. "See! You go ahead and draw a grand prize too if you can!"

"Alright, alright, you're amazing." Li Luo shook his head with a laugh and asked the student, "So what is the grand prize?"

"This is the one and only grand prize." The student opposite him had a solemn expression, but Li Luo felt like the guy was secretly holding back a laugh.

Then everyone saw him lift a large stack of books from under the prize table. With a dull thud, he dropped it heavily onto the table.

"Congratulations, classmate."

The male student said to Ying Chanxi, "This is the grand prize for this event."

Ying Chanxi looked over with curiosity, took a closer look, and was immediately rendered speechless.

—Five Years of Gaokao, Three Years of Mock Exams.

The thick stack of several workbook volumes was beautifully packaged.

But when Li Luo, standing beside her, saw it, he couldn't help but burst out laughing. "No wonder you were the one to win it. It really suits your status as the top student in the grade."

"Get lost!" Ying Chanxi kicked him angrily, then looked at Xu Youyu with a resentful expression. "Senior Sister, what kind of grand prize is this?"

Xu Youyu was also struggling to hold back her laughter. "The grand prize was chosen by the Dean of Students. There's nothing I can do about it. Just accept it. It's the thought that counts, I suppose."

(End of this chapter)
